meta.title: Victoria's payroll tax-free threshold: $700,000 to $1 million (2023-24 Budget)
meta.summary: Worked example (P6): a payroll-tax threshold change. The tax-free threshold rose from $700,000 to $900,000 on 1 July 2024 and to $1 million on 1 July 2025; the threshold is phased out for wages above $3 million (by $1 for every $2) and is nil above $5 million. The rate is 4.85% (metropolitan). Around 6,000 businesses stop paying and more than 26,000 benefit. The Budget's revenue effect, net of the phase-out: +$20.3 million in 2024-25, −$43.6 million in 2025-26 and −$38.7 million in 2026-27.

source.description: Victorian Budget 2023-24, Budget Paper No. 3: Service Delivery, Table 1.27 and p. 114

phaseInYears.note: Two steps: $900,000 from 1 July 2024, $1 million from 1 July 2025

source.description: Victorian Budget 2023-24, Budget Paper No. 3: Service Delivery, Table 1.27 and p. 114

costAbovePerYearDollars.note: Payroll tax at 4.85% on the first $300,000 of wages above the threshold: $0 just above it, up to $14,550 (the saving the Budget gives for businesses that benefit)

source.description: Victorian Budget 2023-24, Budget Paper No. 5: Statement of Finances, chapter 4 (payroll tax)

costAbovePerYearDollars.note: The $1 million deduction is withdrawn by $1 for every $2 of wages above $3 million: from $0 at $3 million to $48,500 of extra tax at $5 million (4.85% × $1 million)

source.description: Victorian Budget 2023-24, Budget Paper No. 3: Service Delivery, Table 1.27 and p. 114
